Business jets, port cranes and paper mills: which Savannah NDT jobs use SNT-TC-1A and which use NAS 410

Gulfstream Aerospace is headquartered at Savannah/Hilton Head International Airport and builds its business jets there, and in July 2024 it opened Savannah Service Center East, adding room to service 26 more aircraft at once. Around that campus sit parts suppliers, maintenance shops and a fast-growing port, with mills, an LNG terminal and power stations a short drive away. The personnel standard behind your certification depends on which of these you work for, not on the method you inspect with. The general rules are compared in NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A.

Savannah-area workDocument you will usually meetWhat decides it
Machining, sheet metal, composite and special process suppliers to airframe programs around Pooler and the airportNAS 410, or EN 4179 on European ordersThe purchase-order quality clause, which flows down to each sub-tier shop that tests the hardware
Business-jet maintenance at manufacturer service centers and independent repair stationsWhatever the repair station's manual and its customer contracts nameThe FAA does not certify NDT personnel; AC 65-31B accepts NAS 410, ATA Specification 105, SNT-TC-1A and other standards
Army aviation at Hunter Army AirfieldService directives and contract termsThe unit and its contracts, not the individual technician
Cranes, spreaders and terminal steel at Garden City and Ocean TerminalA written practice built on SNT-TC-1AAWS D1.1 and the port owner's specifications
The Elba Island LNG terminal, pulp and paper mills, Plant McIntosh and Plant VogtleSNT-TC-1A, sometimes CP-189ASME, API and National Board work; nuclear sites add their own quality-assurance requirements

The aircraft maker's own inspection departments certify under the company's written practice. Ask its Level 3 which standard and revision apply rather than reading the answer off a job advert.

From the crane yard to an airframe supplier

Picture an MT and UT Level II who has spent three years on crane welds at the port and takes a job inspecting machined aluminum details for a jet program. The new employer cannot simply copy the old certificate. Its Responsible Level 3 (RL3) reads the training records, experience log and examination history, decides what to credit, and certifies the technician again under its own program. Expect two gaps. Eddy current and penetrant, the everyday methods on light-alloy structure and fastener holes, may be new. And where the program is written to NAS 410, the surface methods need more formal, documented training than SNT-TC-1A recommends, with approved outlines and recorded hours. Starting that conversation with complete paperwork shortens it.

Veterans leaving Hunter and Fort Stewart

Soldiers who inspected helicopters or ground equipment leave with real skill and a military qualification that a civilian employer does not adopt automatically. Before separating, ask for copies of training transcripts and any documented NDT hours, and keep them with a recent vision examination. A civilian RL3 or Level III can credit what is documented; what is not written down usually has to be repeated.

For quality managers near the airport

Savannah suppliers often run aerospace orders beside port or mill work. State the governing standard and its revision on every certification, keep the training, experience, examination and vision evidence for each inspector in one file, and set a plan for moving a NAS 410 program to Revision 6, released in December 2025, when customers ask. Nadcap AC7114 auditors and customer auditors select real inspectors and trace each one back to that evidence. Atlantis prepares and reviews NAS 410 audit documentation for your RL3 to approve, and the Savannah aerospace consulting page covers written practices built on SNT-TC-1A and aligned to the customer's flow-down and Nadcap AC7114.

Atlantis's part in Savannah

Training follows ASNT SNT-TC-1A: theory online at your own pace with an ASNT NDT Level III on hand for questions, practice in the Practical NDT simulator, and the hands-on work and practical examination at your employer's facility under its written practice. There is no Atlantis classroom in Savannah. For aircraft work the aerospace NDT training page for Savannah sets out the route, and eddy current testing training covers the method most new airframe inspectors add. You can check your theory first with the free Level II practice tests.

A clear line for Savannah readers: Atlantis does not provide NAS 410 training, certification, examinations or a Responsible Level 3. Whether SNT-TC-1A-based training will count toward a NAS 410 certification is for the employer's RL3 to decide, so put the question to that person before enrolling.
